executive_assessment.text: Delta evidence distinguishes climate-income associations, modeled poverty risks and migration as a possible coping strategy, with separate nonrepresentative child consultations in Bac Lieu, Ca Mau and Soc Trang.
Northern Yagi evidence identifies specific protection mechanisms through WASH access and livelihood hardship, without turning planning risks into confirmed violence or trafficking incidents.
Response evidence documents evacuation, multisector assistance and feedback mechanisms rather than evaluated protection or avoided-loss outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-07 reports: Surveyed children identified environmental damage, heat, storms, floods, drought and salt intrusion; 89.9% in Ca Mau cited environmental damage.
Source dated 2025-07 reports: Among surveyed students, 48.2% reported climate-related crop loss, 33.5% poverty risk, and 29.5% interrupted schooling or dropout.
Source dated 2025-07 reports: Soc Trang consultations linked drought and salinity to crop and income losses, work migration and schooling disruption for children left behind.
Source dated 2025-07 reports: Three-province findings identify missing child-specific indicators and targets in climate frameworks; schools and local authorities use participation mechanisms.
Source dated 2025-12 reports: UNICEF and government partners combined WASH, learning, protection and cash support, using child and family feedback to adjust recovery assistance.
Source dated 2024-09-27 reports: The plan says Yagi reversed development gains and deepened hardship in poor affected provinces, increasing human-trafficking risk.

known_gaps.text: No reviewed source established a climate-to-armed-conflict pathway or that armed violence obstructed adaptation; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.
The World Bank climate-income findings are Mekong Delta-wide associations and simulations, not estimates for each province or proof of causality.
UNICEF's climate perceptions are based on a school sample in three delta provinces and should not be read as population prevalence.
Typhoon Yagi reports describe disaster-related trafficking and gender-based violence risks, not confirmed incidents caused by the event.
The updated 2025 National Adaptation Plan PDF at UNFCCC was too large for the browser reader; no claims were taken from indexed snippets.
Geographic names refer to source-era provinces and the 2024 survey/response, before the 2025 administrative reorganization; they are not represented as a current province roster.
Student perceptions from six schools in three delta provinces are not representative province-level exposure or loss rates. Migration is multi-causal and is not itself FCV.
Protection pathways identify risk/exposure, not measured GBV or trafficking increases. No armed-conflict or reverse FCV-to-climate pathway was established in the reviewed sources.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
